guard: nothing typed at a terminal with no session reaches the agent, and the detach key still works there
completionMarker: K. a detach pressed while a FAULTED session is being HANDED BACK is still a keypress
why: EVERY CELL HERE RUNS THE BINARY, so every command builds first. The suite drives `tsx
bin/cotal.ts`, and `@cotal-ai/cli` resolves to `dist/`, so a mutation on `src` that is not built
is a mutation the run never sees: it would come back SURVIVED and read as `this line does not
matter` when what was measured is `this line was not in the artifact`. `dist/` is gitignored, so
git cannot be the recovery for it either, hence the rebuild in every `afterRestore`.
THE SET IS AIMED AT THE WITNESS CELLS, NOT AT THE BOUNDARY ONES. Cells A and B (typed during a
WAIT, typed during an attempt that FAILS) pass with this whole change reverted: the old watcher
owned the wait, and an attempt that fails is followed by a wait whose watcher reads and drops
what was typed. They are in the suite as the boundary of the claim, and nothing here is aimed at
them, because a kill there would say the fix matters when the old code passes the same cell.
Cells C, E, F and G are the ones whose behaviour the change actually inverts.
RUN, NOT PREDICTED: every mutation below KILLED on its named assertion, in a detached copy of
`b67b1e65` with the CLI rebuilt before every run. Progress marks against a 37-mark baseline: 32,
ONE MORE MUTATION WAS RUN AND SURVIVED, and it is recorded here rather than committed, because a
kill set that ships a deliberate survivor exits non-zero for everyone who runs it afterwards and
trains readers to ignore the verdict. Deleting `if (reconnect) ownStdin()` from the session's
`finally` (agents.ts) leaves the suite fully green. That is a REAL coverage gap and the positive
control for it is in the same run: another mutation in the same file was KILLED, so the suite
provably reaches that file at runtime. What the line buys is narrow, and the reason nothing here
grades it is worth more than a kill would be: the backoff wait installs the same reader a moment
later, so the line only covers the window between a session ending and that wait starting, and in
every fault this harness can produce the connection is ALREADY CLOSED when the session ends, so
the hand-back's flush is skipped and the window is a few statements wide. The case the line exists
for is a session that ends transport-class while the SOCKET is still alive (a rail stall), where
the flush runs to its 5s deadline and the keyboard would have no owner for all of it. This harness
cannot produce that: a severed or held link closes the client's connection first. The line stays,
with the same statement in its comment, and the gap is named rather than papered over.
AND ONE MORE, run against every suite that drives a LONE detach byte into a live session through
`runAttachLoop`: deleting the `takeStdin?.()` handoff from `attachClient`'s `onReady`, which leaves
BOTH readers installed during a session. Enumerated rather than assumed (attach.smoke.ts tests the
key parser on hand-built input and attach-repaint drives the manager's own face, so attach-reconnect
and this suite are the two that reach the line). Its disposition is recorded in the PR that added
it; the reachable difference is a press landing in the same instant the link dies, which is the
class we do not build machinery for.

mutations.name: the fix reverted for exactly the establishment window: the reader is stopped before each attempt
mutations.find: const attempting = establishAttachSession(vv, pin, reconnect, first);
mutations.replace:
releaseStdin();
    const attempting = establishAttachSession(vv, pin, reconnect, first);
mutations.expectRed: ...and the seat read nothing of what was typed while the session was being established
mutations.cell: C. bytes typed during an attempt that SUCCEEDS never reach the agent
mutations.note: The shipped defect restored, in the shape it actually had: the old code stopped the watcher and paused stdin before each attempt, so bytes typed while a session was being established buffered and were flushed into the seat by `attachClient`'s own `stdin.resume()`. `releaseStdin()` rather than `idle?.stop()` on purpose, so the next wait builds a FRESH reader exactly as the old code did: a mutant that leaves a stopped reader in place is not the old behaviour, and it would redden cells A and B, which the old code passed. MEASURED at the tip it grades, by hand, with the suite's full output captured rather than inferred from a mark count: A and B stay GREEN, C reddens on the assertion named here with the nonce visible in the seat's own sink, and D reddens twice, on the recorded SIGINT and on the seat's pid being gone. E, F and G are then UNREACHED rather than green: the mutant's own defect killed the agent, so the next cell's attach refuses with `no agent "stdinseat"` and the suite ends there. Unreached is not passed, and the boundary claim above rests on A and B, which did run.

mutations.name: the detach key is not read while a session is being established
mutations.expectRed: the press ends the attach, though it landed with no session to detach from
mutations.cell: E. the detach key struck in that same window ends the attach and hands the slot back
mutations.note: Disarms the race between the in-flight establishment and the press by giving the press a promise that never settles, which is the whole of the second half of this change. Without it the press is not a detach at all: the session that was being established opens, and the attach carries on running with a slot the operator thought they had given back. Anchored on the ONE code line rather than on the block, because a block wide enough to be unique swept up five comment lines and a prose tidy could then disarm the guard silently (the repo's fixture check refuses that, and was right to).

mutations.name: a session that lands behind the press is forgotten instead of handed back
mutations.find: abandoned.push({ grant: late.grant, creds: late.creds, inbox: late.inbox, server: late.server });
mutations.expectRed: ...and the manager is back on the session count it started with, with no slot left behind
mutations.cell: E. the detach key struck in that same window ends the attach and hands the slot back
mutations.note: Ownership, graded on the manager's own live-session count rather than on anything the client says. The seat this suite uses is SILENT, so nothing on the serving side reaps that session for us: the count coming back to base is the client's hand-back or nobody's. This is the assertion that makes the late-landing session a slot returned rather than a slot leaked.

mutations.name: the between-sessions reader SCANS for the detach byte instead of matching one alone
mutations.find: const onData = (d: Buffer) => { if (d.length === 1 && d[0] === byte) hit(); };
mutations.expectRed: the attach is still up: the chunk is not a keypress
mutations.cell: F. a detach byte sharing a read with another byte is not a detach, and is not delivered
mutations.note: The exact-match decision, stated as a mutation. A chunk carrying 0x1d alongside anything else is a paste or a reader that was not reading, never a keypress: measured on a pty, a real keypress arrives in a read of its own even at 3ms spacing. Widening the test to a scan makes a paste end someone's attach, and the cell catches it because the attach exits where it should have stayed up.

mutations.name: the session's own reader SCANS for the detach byte instead of matching one alone
mutations.cell: G. the same chunk in a LIVE session is data, forwarded to the agent, and still not a detach
mutations.note: The same decision on the other side of the handoff, and the cost of it: in a LIVE session a chunk containing 0x1d is DATA and goes to the agent with the byte in it. Widening the test here turns that paste into a detach. Both readers are mutated separately on purpose: one test passing is not evidence about the other, and they are in different packages.

mutations.name: the handoff swallows a press that landed while the session was opening
mutations.expectRed: the press ends the attach, though it landed while the session was opening
mutations.cell: H. the detach key pressed while the new session is OPENING still detaches
mutations.note: Restores the swallow review found: the caller's reader owns stdin until the handoff, the handoff runs when the session is READY, and a press in between is seen by that reader and awaited by nobody. This mutation is also cell H's PREMISE CHECK: with the swallow back, the cell can only pass if the press landed after ready, which is not the window it is aiming at, so the kill is what proves the aim. It needs the suite's slow link to be reachable at all: on loopback the window is under a millisecond wide.

mutations.name: the first attach does not own the keyboard, so what is typed before it comes up is flushed into the seat
mutations.expectRed: ...and the seat read nothing of what was typed before it came up
mutations.cell: I. bytes typed before the FIRST attach comes up never reach the agent either
mutations.note: The reader used to be installed only from the first RECONNECT onwards, which left the commonest path of all uncovered: an attach that has not come up yet is an attach with no session, and everything typed at the terminal while the first establishment ran buffered in the paused stream and was flushed into the seat by the session's own resume. Deleting the line restores exactly that. This mutation must leave cell J green: a pipe is not supposed to have a reader, and a mutation that reddened both would be measuring the gate's existence rather than its position.

mutations.name: the first attach owns a PIPE too, so a script's input is eaten before the session opens
mutations.expectRed: the agent receives what the script wrote
mutations.cell: J. with stdin a PIPE, what was written before the session opened still arrives
mutations.note: The other half of the same gate, and the reason the condition is on the POPULATION rather than on the moment. Widen the reader to every stdin and `printf 'ls\n' | cotal attach` loses its command to a reader that drops what it reads, with no fault anywhere in sight and nothing on screen to say so. The two mutations are a pair on purpose: one says the gate must exist, the other says it must be exactly this gate.
